objectives: Demonstrate accurate decoding, fluency and comprehension of taught ir words.
Explain how ir represents the taught r-controlled vowel sound.
Check accuracy by rereading the whole word or sentence.
concepts: ir represents the taught r-controlled vowel sound
R-controlled vowel patterns are read as taught sound units.
Readers blend consonants and check the complete word for meaning.
Fresh examples test transfer beyond memorised responses.

definitions.definition: A vowel spelling whose sound is influenced by the following r.
Using letter-sound knowledge to read a written word.
Applying a learned skill to a new example.

workedExamples.prompt: Read “bird”. Which spelling represents the r-controlled vowel?
workedExamples.solution: The letters ir represent the taught r-controlled vowel sound.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner reads “shirt” with the wrong vowel sound. What should be checked?
workedExamples.solution: Notice ir and reread the word as a whole.

workedExamples.prompt: Why try a fresh example after guided practice?
workedExamples.solution: A new item checks whether the learner can use the skill independently.

commonMistakes: Splitting the r-controlled vowel into unrelated sounds.
Ignoring r when reading the vowel pattern.
Guessing without blending the complete word.
Advancing without checking accuracy on fresh examples.
